chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ibrahim al-Karkhi, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah عليه السلام: 'I enter into partnership with a polytheist non-Muslim, such that the land, cattle, and seed are from me, while the non-Muslim is responsible for supervision, effort, and work in the cultivation until it becomes wheat or barley. Then the division takes place, the authority takes its share, and what remains is left such that one-third of it is for the non-Muslim and the rest is for me.'
So he عليه السلام said: 'There is no harm in that.'
I said: 'Then is he required to return to me what I put forth of the seed, and then divide the remainder?'
He عليه السلام said: 'No. You only entered into partnership with him on the basis that the seed, cattle, and land are from you, while the supervision and effort are upon him.'

key_terms.الثُّلُثَ: one-third share allocated to the working partner
key_terms.السَّعْيُ: the labor and effort expended in cultivation
key_terms.الْأَرْضُ: the land supplied by the questioner for cultivation
key_terms.الْبَذْرُ: the seed contributed by the questioner as part of the partnership capital
key_terms.الْعِلْجَ: a non-Muslim foreigner, here referring to the polytheist partner
key_terms.الْقِسْمَةُ: the division of the harvested produce
key_terms.الْقِيَامُ: the undertaking or management responsibility borne by the working partner
key_terms.الْمُشْرِكَ: one who associates partners with Allah, describing the partner in this case

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Shia fiqh to enter a crop-sharing partnership with a non-Muslim worker when one party provides the land and seed and the other provides labor?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on an agricultural partnership in which one party provides the land, cattle, and seed, while the other provides labor and management. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام rules that such an arrangement is permissible and clarifies that the seed cost is not to be separately repaid when the partnership was formed on those terms.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.3898 - Al-Hasan bin Mahbub narrated from Ibrahim Al-Karkhi who said: 
I said to Abu Abdillah (as): "I partner with a non-Muslim (al-ilj) in such a way that the land, cattle, and seeds are provided by me, and the non-Muslim is responsible for managing, working, and cultivating the crops until they become wheat or barley. Afterward, harvest is divided, the authorities take their share, and from the remaining portion, the non-Muslim receives one-third while I take the rest."
Imam (as) said: "There is no harm in that."
I then asked: "Is he required to return to me what I spent on the seeds and then divide the remaining harvest?"
Imam (as) said: "No. You partnered with him based on the agreement that the seeds, cattle, and land are provided by you, while he is responsible for the labor and effort."
